sentences.text:
The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Revision Case No.1548 Of 2011
Order:

This Criminal Revision Case is filed by the revision petitioner/accused against the judgment dated 22.07.2011, passed in Crl.A.No.45 of 2010 by the learned Special Sessions Judge for SC/ST Cases cum-VII- Additional District and Sessions Judge at Warangal (for short 'the appellate Court'),
confirming the judgment dated 28.01.2010 passed in C.C.No.178 of 2008 by the learned III Additional Judicial Magistrate of I Class, Warangal (for short 'the trial Court').

2. Briefly, the case against the revision petitioner is that he collected Rs.1,20,000/- from PWs.1 and 2 on the promise that he would get employment Visa in Malaysia for PW.2, who is the husband of PW.1.
However, having collected the amount he failed to get the employment Visa but a visiting Visa was arranged.
Since the employment Visa, was not arranged as promised, PWs.1 and 2 sought return of amount of Rs.1,20,000/-.
The said amount was not returned by the revision petitioner, for which reason a criminal complaint was filed against the revision petitioner.

The police investigated the case and filed charge sheet for the offences punishable under Sections 420 and 506 of The Indian Penal Code (for short 'I.P.C.').
3.

Both the trial Court as well as the appellate Court found the revision petitioner guilty of the offences punishable under Sections 420 and 506 of I.P.C and sentenced him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years and to pay a fine of Rs.2,000/-, in default to suffer simple imprisonment for four months for the offence punishable under Section 420 of I.P.C. and also sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for six months and to pay a fine of Rs.500/-, in default to suffer simple imprisonment for one month for the offence punishable under Section 506 of I.P.C,
which was confirmed by the appellate Court.
4.
Learned counsel appearing for the revision petitioner would submit that the alleged incident of inducement has taken place in the year 2002, however, the complaint was filed in the year 2006.
Since there is a delay of nearly four years, the complaint is barred under Section 468 of Cr.P.C as the complaint was filed beyond limitation period.

5. The punishment prescribed for the offences under Section 420 of I.P.C is maximum of seven (07)
years.
The provisions of Section 468 Cr.P.C. would apply to the offences categorized punishable up to three years.
For the said reason, the ground of limitation is not applicable in the present case.
Learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in M. N. G. Bharateesh Reddy vs. Ramesh Ranganathan and Another 1.

entities.text: M. N. G. Bharateesh Reddy vs. Ramesh Ranganathan and Another 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court while dealing with the case of cheating held that mere breach of contract is not cheating.

In the present facts of the case, it is apparent that the accused having knowledge that he cannot secure a job visa, misrepresented and induced PWs.1 and 2 to part with 1.2 lakhs, causing wrongful loss to them.
Fraudulent intent was from the inception.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the revision petitioner alternatively submitted that the issues have been settled between the parties and further the revision petitioner is now a public servant and any confirmation of conviction would result in revision petitioner losing his job.
The revision petitioner has 2022 SCC Online SC 1061 wife, parents and a son who is disabled i.e., suffering with autistic disease.
He needs regular treatment and attention.

7. Keeping in view the mitigating circumstances and that according to the learned counsel, the issues have been settled in between the parties, this Court is inclined to invoke the provision of 360(4) of Cr.P.C, taking into consideration the Medical Certificate issued by the Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Hospital, Warangal, Telangana State.

The sentence of imprisonment imposed under Sections 420 and 506 of I.P.C are hereby set aside, directing the petitioner to execute a bond of Rs.50,000/- to keep good behaviour for a period of one year, before the concerned Magistrate.
8.
Accordingly, the Criminal Revision Case is allowed.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.

K.SURENDER, J Date: 15.07.2024 vsu Polepaka Jayakar Rao vs The State Of A.P. on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123347060/
